title: Statistics - Conceptual Understanding and Data Transformation
topic: Statistics - Cumulative Frequency, Spread, and Data Effects
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: A cumulative frequency curve is very steep around the median. What does this indicate about the data?
options: Data is tightly clustered around the median
Data is widely spread around the median
questions.explanation: A steep gradient on a cumulative frequency curve means a small range of values contains many data points, indicating tight clustering (small IQR).

questions.question: Two cumulative frequency curves intersect at the 50% cumulative frequency line. What does this imply?
questions.explanation: The 50% cumulative frequency corresponds to the median. If curves intersect there, both data sets have the same median value.

questions.question: A data set has mean = 40, SD = 6. If every value is multiplied by 3, what is the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Multiplying all values by k multiplies the standard deviation by |k|. New SD = 3 × 6 = 18.

questions.question: Which measure of spread is most resistant to extreme outliers?
questions.explanation: The IQR uses only the middle 50% of data (Q1 to Q3), so extreme values at the ends do not affect it. Range and SD are sensitive.

questions.question: A box-and-whisker plot has a much longer right whisker than left whisker. What does this suggest?
questions.explanation: A long right whisker indicates the upper 25% of data is spread over a wider range, creating a tail to the right (positive skew).

questions.question: Given Σx = 150, Σx² = 2500, and n = 10, what is the standard deviation?
The highest value in a data set is removed. Which measure is guaranteed to change?
questions.explanation: Range = Max - Min. Removing the maximum definitely changes the Max, thus changing the Range. Median, Mode, and IQR may remain unchanged.

questions.question: A cumulative frequency curve is flatter in the middle section. What does this suggest?
options: Data is spread out around the median
Data is clustered around the median
questions.explanation: A flat gradient means a large range of values is needed to accumulate frequency, indicating data is spread out (less consistent) in that region.

questions.question: If every value in a data set is decreased by 10, how does the standard deviation change?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation measures spread. Shifting all data by a constant (translation) does not change distances between values, so spread measures remain unchanged.

questions.question: Given Σ(x - x̄)² = 180 and n = 20, what is the standard deviation?
On a cumulative frequency curve, the lower quartile is found at what percentage of total frequency?
questions.explanation: The lower quartile (Q1) is the 25th percentile, found at 25% of the total cumulative frequency.

questions.question: A teacher corrects an error: one score was recorded as 20 instead of 80. How does this affect the mean?
questions.explanation: Correcting 20 to 80 increases the sum of scores. Since Mean = Sum/n, increasing the sum increases the mean.

questions.question: Which statement about standard deviation is correct?
options: SD is always zero or positive
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is calculated using squared distances, so it is always non-negative (≥ 0). It equals zero only when all values are identical.

questions.question: Two classes have identical means. Class X has IQR = 8, Class Y has IQR = 20. Which class has more consistent scores in the middle 50%?
questions.explanation: A smaller IQR indicates the middle 50% of scores are more tightly clustered. Class X (IQR=8) has more consistent middle scores.

questions.question: A cumulative frequency curve for Class A lies entirely to the right of Class B's curve. What does this indicate?
options: Class A has lower scores overall
Class A has higher scores overall
questions.explanation: If Curve A is to the right of Curve B, for any given cumulative frequency percentage, Class A has a higher corresponding value. This indicates Class A generally has higher scores.
